newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian PM confident of poll lead over Labor.
newsitem.headline: Australian PM confident of poll lead over Labor.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard was confident that his Liberal-National coalition government had regained its lead over the Labor Party Opposition, a coalition spokesman said on Tuesday.

He said Howard told a meeting of coalition members that opinion polls showed the government had recovered from several political hiccups over the past few months and was now well ahead of the Australian Labor Party (ALP) again.

"He said that we'd gone through some difficult times over the past couple of months, but it was clear that things were stabilising again and that our lead over the ALP had essentially returned," the spokesman quoted Howard as saying.
The Australian newspaper's Newspoll on Tuesday showed the government had widened its lead over the opposition to eight points from six points two weeks ago.
Support for the government rose one point to 44 percent, while support for the Opposition fell one point to 36 percent.

Mid-way through its first three-year term, the government has been beset by a range of political woes, including stubbornly high unemployment and damaging national rows over Aboriginal land rights, immigration and race.
